first_line: Savior of the heathen, come
note: 'heathen' where later versions have 'nations' (TLH 95: 'Savior of the nations, come'), as the reviewer notes

first_line: The day is surely drawing near
The only Son from heaven
tune: HERR CHRIST, DER EINIG GOTTS SOHN

first_line: To Jordan came our Lord, the Christ
tune: CHRIST UNSER HERR ZUM JORDAN KAM
note: Luther's hymn on Baptism, which TLH lacks

first_line: O Jesus Christ, all praise to Thee
note: TLH 80's version opens 'All praise to Thee, eternal God'

first_line: To God the anthem raising
tune: VON GOTT WILL ICH NICHT LASSEN (Erfurt)

first_line: To the Name of our salvation
The newborn Child this early morn
tune: ICH KOMM AUS FREMDEN LANDEN HER

first_line: Now sing we, now rejoice
Praise God the Lord, ye sons of men
Happy the man who feareth God
note: Luther's Psalm 128, 'Wohl dem, der in Gottes Furcht steht'

first_line: Why art thou cast down, my soul?
Lord, hear the voice of my complaint
note: Agricola's 'Ich ruf zu dir, Herr Jesu Christ', which TLH lacks

first_line: In heav'n is joy and gladness
O wondrous type, O vision fair
note: between Epiphany 5 and Septuagesima, on the last Sunday after the Epiphany

first_line: Salvation unto us has come
May God bestow on us His grace
If Thy beloved Son, O God
When o'er my sins I sorrow
tune: HERR CHRIST, DER EINIG GOTTS SOHN
note: to HERR CHRIST, DER EINIG GOTTS SOHN, not to a tune of its own (WENN MEINE SÜND)

first_line: O Christ, who art the light and day
note: TLH 559's first line, from the Latin 'Christe qui lux es et dies'; ELHB 34, from the German 'Christe, der du bist Tag und Licht', opens the same way

first_line: O faithful God, we worship Thee
A mighty fortress is our God
Christ, the Life of all the living
Lord Jesus Christ, true man and God
note: Eber's 'Herr Jesu Christ, wahr Mensch und Gott'

first_line: Lamb of God, pure and holy
The death of Jesus Christ, our Lord
O sacred Head, now wounded
Ere yet the dawn hath filled the skies
Christ Jesus lay in death's strong bands
Ye sons and daughters of the King
note: 'daughers' in the list as given

first_line: The Lord's my Shepherd, I'll not want
note: the Scottish Psalter's Psalm 23

first_line: Zion mourns in fear and anguish
Look down, O Lord, from heav'n, behold
note: Luther's Psalm 12; TLH 260 opens 'O Lord, look down from heaven, behold'

first_line: Our Father, Thou in heav'n above
Dear Christians, one and all rejoice
Had God not come, may Israel say
note: Luther's Psalm 124, 'Wär Gott nicht mit uns diese Zeit'; to a tune the reviewer likens to WO GOTT DER HERR NICHT BEI UNS HÄLT, which Hymnary.org gives as GUD, DU AF INGA SKIFTEN VET

first_line: Come, Holy Ghost, God and Lord
We all believe in one true God
tune: WIR GLAUBEN ALL AN EINEN GOTT, VATER
note: Clausnitzer's hymn on the Apostles' Creed, 'Wir glauben all an einen Gott, Vater', not Luther's creed hymn (TLH 251)

first_line: From God shall naught divide me
tune: VON GOTT WILL ICH NICHT LASSEN (Erfurt)

first_line: The mouth of fools doth God confess
note: Luther's Psalm 14

first_line: In Thee alone, O Christ, my Lord
note: to ALLEIN ZU DIR in an isometric form

first_line: Lord Jesus Christ, Thou highest good
note: Ringwaldt's penitential hymn, 'Herr Jesu Christ, du höchstes Gut, du Brunnquell aller Gnaden'

first_line: My inmost heart now raises
That man a godly life might live
note: Luther's Ten Commandments

first_line: Wondrous King, all-glorious
The will of God is always best
Oh, blest the house, whate'er befall
My Jesus, as Thou wilt
note: to DENBY, not to JEWETT (TLH 420's tune)

first_line: All mankind fell in Adam's fall
O Christ, our true and only Light
tune: O JESU CHRIST, MEINS LEBENS LICHT

first_line: Jesus, priceless Treasure
Show pity, Lord! O Lord, forgive
note: Isaac Watts's Psalm 51

first_line: Why art thou thus cast down, my heart
tune: WARUM BETRÜBST DU DICH, MEIN HERZ
lexicon: Warum betrübst du dich, mein Herz
note: the lexicon's English title of 'Warum betrübst du dich, mein Herz', whose tune it has; the Lutheran Hymn Index has no row for it

first_line: Now lay we calmly in the grave
In Thee, Lord, have I put my trust
Thee Lord, our God, we praise
note: Luther's Te Deum, 'Herr Gott, dich loben wir'; ELHal 356 opens the same way, on a row of its own in the index

first_line: We all believe in one true God
tune: WIR GLAUBEN ALL AN EINEN GOTT, VATER
note: the hymn of 38 again

first_line: How lovely shines the morning star
By grace I'm saved, grace free and boundless
From depths of woe I cry to Thee
For help, O(h) whither shall I flee
note: 'O(h)' as the list gives it

first_line: In God, my faithful God
When in the hour of utmost need
Now thank we all our God
The Bridegroom soon will call us
note: the last of the Sundays; the saints' days follow, numbered with gaps (66 is wanting)

first_line: Rejoice, all ye believers
Sweet flowerets of the martyr band
Zion stands by hills surrounded
O Thou, who dost accord us
note: from the Latin 'Summi largitor praemii'

first_line: Lord of the Church, we humbly pray
In peace and joy I now depart
Look from Thy sphere of endless day
All glory be to God on high

occasion: Presentation of the Augsburg Confession (25 June)
first_line: My Church! My Church! My dear old Church
Lord God, we all to Thee give praise
Christ is our Corner-stone
Jesus calls us; o'er the tumult
note: no day in the list. Cecil Frances Alexander wrote it for St Andrew's Day (30 Nov), which would stand here, after All Saints, if the saints' days run from December to November; not loaded
